title: the journeys in the browser: purchases to receipt, download and admin, failure, 3-D Secure, cancel, refund with step-up, return, the availability notice, a preorder, a dispute and the owner's switch
readFirst: PLANS/P08-CONTRACT.md: section 11 (the invariants and the test matrix: the journeys row is this round's), sections 7, 9 and 10 (the functions, the emulator's routes and the stand-in page, the public pages and the admin)
PLANS/VERIFICATION.md (the payment, refund, delivery, availability and dispute proofs) and PLANS/WORK-PACKAGES.md (the P08 section)

tests/e2e/cart-checkout.spec.ts (the emulator control helpers `emulatorControl`, the stand-in page's buttons, the return page), tests/e2e/order-page.spec.ts (the order page and the notify link pages), tests/e2e/owner-operations.spec.ts (the jobs endpoint with `JOBS_SECRET` from `localEnv()`, Mailpit search and message reading, TOTP enrolment and the step-up dialog), tests/e2e/orders-admin.spec.ts and tests/e2e/orders-money.spec.ts (rounds 11a and 11b: the admin screens, their seed helpers), tests/e2e/store-admin.spec.ts (round 11c: the variant form's preorder fields and the paid-file upload), tests/e2e/product-availability.spec.ts (round 10b: the product page states and the sign-up), tests/e2e/helpers.ts, playwright.config.ts (the emulator is one of its web servers)
tests/support/moyasar-emulator.ts (every control route: config, pay, payment, invoice, webhook, fault, state, reset) and docs/payments-runbook.md (the emulator section)

artifacts/acceptance/P08/rounds/round-10a.md, round-10b.md, round-11a.md, round-11b.md, round-11c.md: the uncovered cases the auditors listed that a real journey can close (the real file journey through Storage, the real `held` refusal, the real sign-up body, the real refund through the emulator)
brief:
Write `tests/e2e/orders.spec.ts`: the journeys of contract section 11's last row, end to end on the real local stack, the real Edge Functions and the local Moyasar emulator (a test harness; nothing here may reach Moyasar). No `page.route` mock of any function or Data API call in this spec: everything a buyer and the owner do goes through the real pages and the real functions. Each journey runs at 360 and 1440 (two projects of one describe, or a width loop, the way the other specs do), each with its own seeded products so the two widths never share stock. This round writes tests only; a defect a journey finds in product code is reported under contractGaps with its evidence and left alone (the orchestrator rules), unless the fix is inside this round's files.

Setup, once per run: an owner with TOTP enrolled (the owner-operations way), an operations member; checkout switched on and the seller and approved policies in place (the demo catalog's, or set through the service role the way `commerceHarness` does, restored afterwards); products and variants seeded through the service role with unique SKUs: a digital book with a paid file uploaded through the admin's real paid-file flow (round 11c) before the purchase, a physical book, a signed edition, an out-of-stock physical item, a preorder variant (capacity 3, a date 30 days out in Riyadh, a note). The emulator's state is reset at the start (`/__emulator/reset`) and its webhook pointed at the local `payments` function (`/__emulator/config` with `webhookUrl`, `webhookSecret` from the test values the helpers already expose, `autoWebhook: true`, `autoCallback: true`). The receipts and other mail are sent by calling the `outbox` jobs endpoint with `JOBS_SECRET` (from `localEnv()`) and read in Mailpit by a marker unique to the run.

The journeys (each a test, at both widths):
1. A book purchase: the product page, add, the cart, the checkout form, «تأكيد الطلب», the hold view, «ادفع الآن» to the stand-in page, «pay», back on the return page through «جارٍ التحقق من الدفع» to «تم الدفع», the cart cleared. The receipt arrives in Mailpit with the order link; the link opens the order page (the token leaves the address bar); «تنزيل» issues and redeems a real download (the signed Storage URL answers 200 with the file's bytes and `content-type`, checked with `request`, not by opening the file); the owner's `/admin/orders` lists the order as paid and its view shows the verified evidence.
2. A non-book purchase (physical): paid the same way; the owner ships it (carrier and tracking) and marks it delivered; the `order_shipped` mail arrives; the buyer's order page shows the tracking; the buyer files a return request; the owner approves and receives it with a restock (the stock rises).
3. A failed payment: «fail» on the stand-in page leaves the invoice payable; the return page (back) shows the payment still pending; a second try with «pay» settles it once (one paid attempt, one receipt).
4. 3-D Secure: the stand-in page's 3-D Secure step, then success; and a second order whose 3-D Secure step is rejected, which stays unpaid.
5. Cancelled: «إلغاء الطلب» on the hold view before paying; the order is cancelled, the stock is free again (the same quantity can be ordered at once), and a late «pay» forced on the cancelled invoice (`/__emulator/pay` with `force`) lands as a late payment the ledger records honestly (paid or needs resolution per the contract, never lost).
6. A refund with the step-up: the owner refunds one line of a paid order from the order view (the real `refund-create` against the emulator, the TOTP dialog), the refund succeeds, the provider's refunded total in `/__emulator/state` equals the ledger's, the `order_refunded` mail arrives, the buyer's order page shows the refunded amount, and a digital line refunded in full no longer offers a download. A second press of the same confirmation (or a replay with the same idempotency key) reaches the emulator's refund route once.
7. The availability notice: the out-of-stock variant's product page, a real sign-up (the real `notify`, the real Turnstile test key), the confirmation mail, its link on `/notify/confirm`, «تأكيد»; the owner raises the stock in the variant form; the sweep runs (call `finance.availability_sweep()` through the service role's database connection rather than waiting a minute); the `availability` mail arrives once (a second sweep sends nothing more); its unsubscribe link on `/notify/unsubscribe` works and a later restock mails nothing.
8. A preorder: the product page shows «طلب مسبق: يُسلَّم في <date>» and the note, the cart and the checkout show them before payment, the purchase is paid, the order page and the receipt show the preorder note, and the variant form's «طلبات مسبقة مؤكدة» shows 1. Then a buyer whose quantity exceeds the remaining capacity is refused by the quote.
9. A dispute: the owner records a chargeback against a paid attempt through the reconciliation screen's or the order view's form (the step-up), repeats the same row (answered as a duplicate), adds a follow-up; the statistics screen's dispute figures and `owner_commerce_stats` agree, and the order's refunds are untouched.
10. The owner's switch: with checkout switched off through the commerce settings form (the step-up), the checkout page refuses a new order; switched on again, a new order goes through.

Rules: every assertion reads what the page shows or what the real ledger holds (through the service role's database connection, read-only queries), never a mocked reply. Money in halalas, Arabic sentences exact. Save screenshots of each journey's key screens at both widths through `tests/e2e/shots.ts`. Clean up what the spec created where the schema allows it (products and variants it seeded; orders stay, as in every other spec, and the acceptance battery starts from a fresh reset). Keep the spec under about 10 minutes for both widths; reuse one signed-in owner context across the journeys of a width.

Run the dev server only through Playwright's own webServer (the emulator is the config's second web server). Before any e2e run check that at least 10 GB of memory is free; if not, stop leftover headless Chrome processes, and if it is still short report it and skip the e2e run. Copy `next-env.d.ts` aside before an e2e run and restore it after; if `pnpm typecheck` then fails with TS1128 in `.next/e2e`, remove `.next/e2e`.

Never open, read or print a .env file (the repository's, `.env.local` or `supabase/functions/.env`), not even to derive a test value; the test helpers already load what a test needs. No network call to Moyasar.
checks: pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/orders.spec.ts (memory check first; base URL http://localhost:3000), run twice in a row: the second run must pass too (nothing left behind breaks it)
auditFocus: Does every journey go through the real pages and the real functions with no mock, and does each assertion fail if the behaviour it names breaks (a test that would pass with the payment never settling, the receipt never sent, the refund never reaching the emulator, or the notice sent twice is a finding). Money settles once: one paid attempt, one receipt, one refund call per confirmation, the provider's refunded total equal to the ledger's. The late payment on a cancelled order is recorded, never lost. The download is a real Storage response. The availability notice once per restock, never after the unsubscribe. Both widths, each with its own stock. No call to Moyasar; no .env read; nothing left behind that breaks a second run.
